baseline_report: The patient's persistent cough and visual field defect, together with a 125-pack-year smoking history and prior brain tumor surgery, prompted imaging evaluation. Chest CT showing a 55-mm right upper lobe mass with hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy, and brain MRI showing a 38-mm cystic right occipital lesion, strongly support a single lung-brain metastatic process. This pattern best explains both symptoms and is consistent with the leading hypothesis of lung cancer brain metastasis (confidence 0.72). The alternative of separate brain tumor recurrence plus lung disease is less likely (0.18), and COPD with prior brain tumor sequelae is poorly supported (0.10) because the imaging findings are not typical COPD and the brain lesion is active, not post-surgical change. However, pathological confirmation from lung biopsy and prior brain surgery is still missing, so tissue verification remains necessary to raise confidence further. At present, the clinical and imaging evidence sufficiently converges on lung cancer with brain metastasis.
